chapter: Heroes, heard bands and Lunceford's life on the road
title: Big Sid Catlett caught in Boston
summary: Crawford tells of seeing Sid Catlett run naked down Columbus Avenue after being caught in bed with a Jones brother's wife.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Okay, you brought Sid Catlett up quite

Well, I knew about Sid. Well, I tell you something that happened in Boston. I don't want to say it on tape. I can say it, but I really don't want to say it, and I saw it actually happen. Old Sid Catlett -- we were all staying at Mother's Lunch, and old Sid was caught in the bedroom with, oh, what was the name of the -- one of the Jones Brothers' wife, who -- the wife was the daughter of Mom that owned Mom's lunch in the boarding house, rooming house.

This old Jones Brother came in there. They were a singing group, four of them, three of them, three or four, three of them, and caught Sid in bed with his wife. Man, Sid ran out of that room, down the street, naked as he could be.
Down the street, and this big guy, one of the Jones Brothers was right behind him. Man, you know, this goes on, but Sid was naked as a jaybird.

I'm telling you, that was the funniest thing. I laughed. And he had the nerve to ask me, man, why didn't you help me? Why didn't you come to my rescue? I said, I wasn't in it. I wasn't doing any bad, any wrongs. That was the funniest scene I ever saw in my life, right down Columbus Avenue in Boston, Massachusetts.
So that I'll never forget, which was fun to me. I laughed. And so Big Sid was a great fellow.
